background: NORD/LB is the Landesbank of Lower Saxony and Saxony-Anhalt, owned by the two states and the regional savings banks, a corporate, energy and real-estate lender that was recapitalised after shipping losses and also acts as central bank for its savings banks.
synthesis: Two of the three main agencies rate the bank, at AA- on average and both on a stable outlook, after a one-notch upgrade by one of them on 12 May 2026. Capital is comfortable, with CET1 of 17.4% and leverage of 5.7% both above their peer medians, and short-term liquidity has improved, LCR of 154% above the median and up 18 points since 30 Jun 2025. The weak spot is structural funding: NSFR of 113% is in the bottom quarter of EU and Nordic banks and broadly flat, which is the figure to watch at a wholesale-funded lender. CET1 is up 0.8 points over the same period (figures to 30 Jun 2026), and nothing has been flagged in the last 90 days.
